revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Middle School Fundraiser
revealWordProblem.text: Some sixth-grade students will make 50 bags of honey granola to sell at a fundraising event using the recipe shown. They will put 2 cups of granola in each bag and will sell each bag for $5. Choose one question to answer. Question 1: How many cups of rolled oats will the students need to buy? Question 2: One pound of almonds costs $9.99 and has 3 cups of almonds. How much will the students need to budget for almonds?
revealWordProblem.imageAlt: A can of rolled oats printed with a Honey Granola recipe that makes 6 cups.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: Question 1: The recipe makes 6 cups of granola using 4 cups of rolled oats, so rolled oats to total granola is a 4:6 ratio. The students need 50 bags × 2 cups = 100 cups of granola in all. Scaling the ratio: 100 ÷ 6 × 4 = 66 2/3 cups of rolled oats. They need to buy about 66 2/3 cups of rolled oats.

questions.stem: A recipe uses 4 cups of milk and 1 cup of cream. What is the ratio of milk to cream?
questions.explanation: A ratio compares quantities in the order given. Milk to cream = 4 to 1, or 4:1.
choiceFeedback: The order matters — what is named first should be first in the ratio.
You added the numbers together — a ratio compares two amounts, not their sum.
5 is the total number of cups, not the amount of cream. This compares the whole recipe to one part instead of milk to cream.
hints: Re-read the question: it asks for milk to cream, in that exact order.
In a ratio, the amount named first goes first. Find the milk amount and the cream amount before you write anything.
Underline the two amounts: milk = 4 cups, cream = 1 cup. Write them in the same order the question names them.
questions.stemEs: Una receta usa 4 tazas de leche y 1 taza de crema. ¿Cuál es la razón de leche a crema?
questions.explanationEs: Una razón compara cantidades en el orden que se indica. Leche a crema = 4 a 1, o 4:1.
hintsEs: Vuelve a leer la pregunta: pide leche a crema, exactamente en ese orden.
En una razón, la cantidad que se nombra primero va primero. Halla la cantidad de leche y la de crema antes de escribir nada.
Subraya las dos cantidades: leche = 4 tazas, crema = 1 taza. Escríbelas en el mismo orden en que las nombra la pregunta.

questions.stem: Chef Reyes uses 6 strawberries and 2 bananas in a smoothie. What is the part-to-whole ratio of bananas to total fruit?
questions.explanation: Total fruit = 6 + 2 = 8. The part-to-whole ratio of bananas to total fruit is 2:8.
choiceFeedback: Re-check: does this show a part being compared to the whole group?
This compares bananas to strawberries, which is part-to-part. A part-to-whole ratio needs the total number of pieces of fruit as the second number.
The order matters — what is named first should be first in the ratio.
hints: Notice the word 'total' — this is a part-to-WHOLE ratio, not banana-to-strawberry.
First find the total fruit by adding strawberries and bananas. Then compare bananas to that total.
Add 6 + 2 to get the total fruit. Then write the bananas' number first, followed by that total.
questions.stemEs: El chef Reyes usa 6 fresas y 2 plátanos en un batido. ¿Cuál es la razón parte a todo de plátanos a fruta total?
questions.explanationEs: Fruta total = 6 + 2 = 8. La razón parte a todo de plátanos a fruta total es 2:8.
hintsEs: Fíjate en la palabra 'total': esta es una razón parte a TODO, no de plátano a fresa.
Primero halla la fruta total sumando las fresas y los plátanos. Luego compara los plátanos con ese total.
Suma 6 + 2 para obtener la fruta total. Luego escribe primero el número de plátanos, seguido de ese total.

questions.stem: In a class of 30 students, 18 are girls. What is the part-to-part ratio of boys to girls?
questions.explanation: Boys = 30 − 18 = 12. Part-to-part ratio of boys to girls = 12:18. (Order matters!)
choiceFeedback: The order matters — what is named first should be first in the ratio.
You added the numbers together — a ratio compares two amounts, not their sum.
You found the number of boys correctly, but 30 is the whole class. That makes this part-to-whole, and the question asks boys compared to girls.
hints: The problem tells you girls (18) and the whole class (30) — but it asks about BOYS to girls.
Find the number of boys first by subtracting the girls from the class total. Then write boys first, girls second.
Subtract 30 − 18 to find the boys. Put that number first in the ratio, then 18 for the girls.
questions.stemEs: En una clase de 30 estudiantes, 18 son niñas. ¿Cuál es la razón parte a parte de niños a niñas?
questions.explanationEs: Niños = 30 − 18 = 12. La razón parte a parte de niños a niñas = 12:18. (¡El orden importa!)
hintsEs: El problema te da las niñas (18) y toda la clase (30), pero pregunta por los NIÑOS a las niñas.
Halla primero el número de niños restando las niñas del total de la clase. Luego escribe niños primero y niñas después.
Resta 30 − 18 para hallar los niños. Pon ese número primero en la razón y luego 18 para las niñas.

reviewHighlights.formula: a : b | a to b | a/b
steps: 1. A ratio compares two quantities; order of quantities matters
2. Part-to-Part compares two distinct subgroups (e.g. boys to girls)
3. Part-to-Whole compares one subgroup to the total (e.g. boys to class)
reviewHighlights.watchOut: A common mistake in Understand Ratios is writing the ratio in the wrong order: when asked for the ratio of apple juice to sparkling water in a recipe that uses 3 cups of apple juice for every 2 cups of sparkling water, some students write 2:3 (sparkling water to apple juice) because they list the ingredients in whatever order comes to mind rather than the order the question asks for. The two ratios describe different drinks — 3:2 means 3 cups of juice for every 2 cups of water, while 2:3 would mean only 2 cups of juice for every 3 cups of water. Always match the order of your ratio to the order named in the question: "apple juice to sparkling water" means the apple juice number comes first, giving 3:2.

level1.stem: A pet store has 5 dogs and 9 cats. What is the ratio of dogs to cats?
level1.explanation: The ratio of dogs to cats compares dogs first, then cats: 5 to 9, or 5:9.
choiceFeedback: The order matters — what is named first should be first in the ratio.
You added the numbers together — a ratio compares two amounts, not their sum.
14 is the total number of pets, and here it is written first. Check both the order of the words and whether the question asks about a total at all.
hints: Re-read: the question asks for dogs to cats, in that order.
A ratio only uses the two amounts being compared — don't add them together. Match the order to the words.
Dogs are named first, so their count (5) starts the ratio. Then write the cats' count after the colon.
level1.stemEs: Una tienda de mascotas tiene 5 perros y 9 gatos. ¿Cuál es la razón de perros a gatos?
level1.explanationEs: La razón de perros a gatos compara primero los perros y después los gatos: 5 a 9, o 5:9.
hintsEs: Vuelve a leer: la pregunta pide perros a gatos, en ese orden.
Una razón solo usa las dos cantidades que se comparan; no las sumes. Haz que el orden coincida con las palabras.

level2.stem: A fruit salad has 5 pieces of melon, 3 pieces of pineapple, and 2 grapes. What is the ratio of pineapple to melon?
level2.explanation: The ratio of pineapple to melon compares pineapple (3) to melon (5), so the ratio is 3:5.
choiceFeedback: The order matters — what is named first should be first in the ratio.
That compares pineapple to the total (5 + 3 + 2). The question compares pineapple to melon only.
You started with the pineapple, which fits the order — but 2 is the number of grapes. Re-read which two amounts the question compares.
hints: Three fruits are listed, but the question only compares pineapple and melon — the grapes are extra info.
Pick out just the two amounts you need, then write them in the order the question names: pineapple first.
Circle the pineapple count (3) and the melon count (5). Write them in the order 'pineapple to melon.'
level2.stemEs: Una ensalada de frutas tiene 5 trozos de melón, 3 trozos de piña y 2 uvas. ¿Cuál es la razón de piña a melón?
level2.explanationEs: La razón de piña a melón compara la piña (3) con el melón (5), así que la razón es 3:5.
hintsEs: Se mencionan tres frutas, pero la pregunta solo compara piña y melón — las uvas son información de más.
Escoge solo las dos cantidades que necesitas y escríbelas en el orden que nombra la pregunta: la piña primero.
Encierra la cantidad de piña (3) y la de melón (5). Escríbelas en el orden 'piña a melón'.

level2.stem: A parking lot has 10 cars and 6 trucks. What is the part-to-whole ratio of trucks to total vehicles?
level2.explanation: Total vehicles = 10 + 6 = 16. The ratio of trucks to total is 6:16.
choiceFeedback: Re-check: does this show a part being compared to the whole group?
This compares trucks to cars, which is a part-to-part ratio. For part-to-whole you need 10 + 6 as the second number.
The order matters — what is named first should be first in the ratio.
hints: The word 'total' means this is part-to-whole — compare trucks to ALL vehicles, not to cars.
First find the total number of vehicles by adding cars and trucks. The trucks' number goes first.
Add 10 + 6 to find the total vehicles. Then write 6 (the trucks) first and that total second.
level2.stemEs: Un estacionamiento tiene 10 autos y 6 camionetas. ¿Cuál es la razón parte a todo de camionetas al total de vehículos?
level2.explanationEs: Total de vehículos = 10 + 6 = 16. La razón de camionetas al total es 6:16.
hintsEs: La palabra 'total' significa que esto es parte a todo: compara los camiones con TODOS los vehículos, no con los carros.
Primero halla el número total de vehículos sumando carros y camiones. El número de camiones va primero.
Suma 10 + 6 para hallar el total de vehículos. Luego escribe 6 (los camiones) primero y ese total después.

11 is the total number of cups, not an ingredient. Part-to-part compares the two ingredients themselves.
level2.stemEs: Tazón de preparación A: el chef Reyes mezcla 7 tazas de harina con 4 tazas de agua para hacer masa. ¿Cuál es la razón parte a parte de harina a agua?
level2.explanationEs: Parte a parte compara los dos ingredientes en el orden en que se nombran. Harina a agua = 7 a 4, escrito 7:4.
hints: A ratio compares two amounts in the exact order the question names them.
Part-to-part compares one ingredient directly to the other ingredient, so there is no total to add here.
The question names flour first, so 7 goes in the first spot — now decide which amount belongs after the colon.

Parte a parte compara un ingrediente directamente con el otro, así que aquí no hay que sumar ningún total.

level2.stem: “For every” language: Chef Reyes says, “My glaze uses 9 spoons of honey for every 4 spoons of lemon.” Written in colon notation, the ratio of honey to lemon is:
level2.explanation: “For every 9 honey to 4 lemon” is a part-to-part comparison. In colon notation, honey to lemon is 9:4.
choiceFeedback: The order matters — what is named first should be first in the ratio.
You added the numbers together — a ratio compares two amounts, not their sum.
13 is the total number of spoons, so this compares the whole mixture to the lemon. “For every” language compares the two ingredients themselves.
level2.stemEs: Lenguaje de «por cada»: el chef Reyes dice: «Mi glaseado usa 9 cucharadas de miel por cada 4 cucharadas de limón». En notación con dos puntos, la razón de miel a limón es:
level2.explanationEs: «Por cada 9 de miel a 4 de limón» es una comparación parte a parte. En notación con dos puntos, miel a limón es 9:4.
hints: “For every” is ratio language — it compares one amount directly to another amount.
Colon notation writes the quantity named first, then a colon, then the quantity named second.
The sentence names honey first with 9 spoons, so 9 goes before the colon — now decide which number belongs after it.
hintsEs: «Por cada» es lenguaje de razón: compara una cantidad directamente con otra cantidad.
La notación con dos puntos escribe primero la cantidad que se nombra primero, luego los dos puntos y después la segunda cantidad.
La oración nombra primero la miel con 9 cucharadas, así que el 9 va antes de los dos puntos; ahora decide qué número va después.

level3.stem: A bag of marbles has 8 red, 6 blue, and 4 green marbles. Write three different ratios using these quantities: one part-to-part ratio, one part-to-whole ratio, and explain the difference.
level3.sampleAnswer: Part-to-part: red to blue = 8:6. Part-to-whole: green to total = 4:18. The difference is that part-to-part compares two individual groups, while part-to-whole compares one group to the entire collection (8 + 6 + 4 = 18).
level3.hint: Remember to explain which type each ratio is.
hints: You need THREE things: a part-to-part ratio, a part-to-whole ratio, and an explanation of how they differ.
Part-to-part compares two colors. Part-to-whole compares one color to ALL marbles — so you'll need the total first.
Start by finding the whole: add 8 + 6 + 4. Then pick any two colors for your part-to-part ratio, like red to blue.
level3.stemEs: Una bolsa de canicas tiene 8 canicas rojas, 6 azules y 4 verdes. Escribe tres razones distintas usando estas cantidades: una razón parte a parte, una razón parte a todo, y explica la diferencia.
level3.explanation: A part-to-part ratio compares two groups to each other, such as red to blue, 8:6. A part-to-whole ratio compares one group to the total of 8 + 6 + 4 = 18 marbles, such as green to all marbles, 4:18. The difference is what the second number stands for: another part, or the entire set.
level3.explanationEs: Una razón parte a parte compara dos grupos entre sí, por ejemplo rojas a azules, 8:6. Una razón parte a todo compara un grupo con el total de 8 + 6 + 4 = 18 canicas, por ejemplo verdes a todas las canicas, 4:18. La diferencia está en lo que representa el segundo número: otra parte o el conjunto completo.
hintsEs: Necesitas TRES cosas: una razón parte a parte, una razón parte a todo y una explicación de en qué se diferencian.
Parte a parte compara dos colores. Parte a todo compara un color con TODAS las canicas, así que necesitarás el total primero.
Empieza hallando el todo: suma 8 + 6 + 4. Luego escoge dos colores cualesquiera para tu razón parte a parte, como rojo a azul.

La clase completa son 5 + 7 = 12 estudiantes. Ahora decide qué número nombra primero la pregunta y colócalo antes de los dos puntos.

level3.stem: “For every” language: Chef Reyes says, “My glaze uses 9 spoons of honey for every 4 spoons of lemon.” Written in colon notation, the ratio of honey to lemon is:
level3.explanation: “For every 9 honey to 4 lemon” is a part-to-part comparison. In colon notation, honey to lemon is 9:4.
choiceFeedback: The order matters — what is named first should be first in the ratio.
You added the numbers together — a ratio compares two amounts, not their sum.
13 is the total number of spoons, so this compares the whole mixture to the lemon. “For every” language compares the two ingredients themselves.
level3.stemEs: Lenguaje de «por cada»: el chef Reyes dice: «Mi glaseado usa 9 cucharadas de miel por cada 4 cucharadas de limón». En notación con dos puntos, la razón de miel a limón es:
level3.explanationEs: «Por cada 9 de miel a 4 de limón» es una comparación parte a parte. En notación con dos puntos, miel a limón es 9:4.
hints: “For every” is ratio language — it compares one amount directly to another amount.
Colon notation writes the quantity named first, then a colon, then the quantity named second.
The sentence names honey first with 9 spoons, so 9 goes before the colon — now decide which number belongs after it.
hintsEs: «Por cada» es lenguaje de razón: compara una cantidad directamente con otra cantidad.
La notación con dos puntos escribe primero la cantidad que se nombra primero, luego los dos puntos y después la segunda cantidad.
La oración nombra primero la miel con 9 cucharadas, así que el 9 va antes de los dos puntos; ahora decide qué número va después.

level3.stem: A recipe uses 4 cups of milk and 1 cup of cream. What is the ratio of milk to cream?
level3.explanation: A ratio compares quantities in the order given. Milk to cream = 4 to 1, or 4:1.
choiceFeedback: The order matters — what is named first should be first in the ratio.
You added the numbers together — a ratio compares two amounts, not their sum.
5 is the total number of cups, not the amount of cream. This compares the whole recipe to one part instead of milk to cream.
hints: Re-read the question: it asks for milk to cream, in that exact order.
In a ratio, the amount named first goes first. Find the milk amount and the cream amount before you write anything.
Underline the two amounts: milk = 4 cups, cream = 1 cup. Write them in the same order the question names them.
level3.stemEs: Una receta usa 4 tazas de leche y 1 taza de crema. ¿Cuál es la razón de leche a crema?
level3.explanationEs: Una razón compara cantidades en el orden que se indica. Leche a crema = 4 a 1, o 4:1.
hintsEs: Vuelve a leer la pregunta: pide leche a crema, exactamente en ese orden.
En una razón, la cantidad que se nombra primero va primero. Halla la cantidad de leche y la de crema antes de escribir nada.
Subraya las dos cantidades: leche = 4 tazas, crema = 1 taza. Escríbelas en el mismo orden en que las nombra la pregunta.

tool.title: 20 Cups of Fruit Drink, Made in Equal Batches
tool.caption: One batch of Chef Reyes's recipe is 3 cups of apple juice and 2 cups of sparkling water, so one batch makes 5 cups of fruit drink. A 20-cup punch bowl holds 4 of those equal batches, and each batch carries 3 cups of apple juice, so the bowl needs 4 x 3 = 12 cups of apple juice.
